name: Perception Encoder
plain: Meta's Perception Encoder (T, S, B, L, G): PE-Core image features aligned with text, and PE-Spatial for dense tasks.
summary: Perception Encoder (Bolya et al. 2025, Meta) image towers with 2D RoPE: PE core (contrastive, attention-pool embedding) and PE spatial (dense features for detection / segmentation; no learned pool: pooler_output is the mean of the patch tokens, as timm); tokens at any size.

papers.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of the network

official.reason: timm ports the PE image towers to its common ViT code; the authors' perception_models repo is a full training and eval stack.

limitations: kernels replays a CUDA graph per small input shape without hidden states (up to about 1M activations: ViT-B ~460 px, ViT-L ~300 px), captured on the shape's second call, at most 4 per model; `model.release_graphs()` frees them.

Small kernels calls (graph-sized, with or without `layers`) run GEMMs of at most 600 tokens on cuBLAS: faster in a graph replay (ViT-B/16 224 px: 1.26 against 1.52 ms), about 10 % slower eagerly on ViT-T / B; a replay equals the eager call bit for bit.
`fp32_accumulate = true` puts every GEMM on cuBLAS with fp32 accumulation (the portable precision; slower on GeForce).
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: dense patch features and a pooled image feature.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 16 % and p99 <= 68 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `last_hidden_state`).
